questions.q: What does a trigger dependency actually connect?
options: Two tumbling window triggers — one only fires once the other's dependency window succeeds
Two activities inside the same pipeline
A Schedule trigger and a storage event trigger
Two entirely separate data factories
questions.explain: Trigger dependencies chain tumbling window triggers together, one level up from Chapter 4's activity-level dependency conditions.

questions.q: What does a negative offset mean in a trigger dependency?
options: The dependency window sits earlier than the dependent trigger's own window — the common "wait for yesterday" pattern
The dependency is disabled
The dependent trigger will never actually fire
The offset value is always ignored when negative
questions.explain: A negative offset means the dependency's window comes before the dependent trigger's window — for example, waiting for yesterday's data before running today's aggregation.

questions.q: What is self-dependency, and what offset does it require?
options: A trigger depending on its own earlier runs, always requiring a negative offset
A trigger depending on itself with no offset restrictions at all
A feature only available on Schedule triggers
A way to disable retries on a trigger
questions.explain: Self-dependency keeps a trigger's windows strictly sequential — each window waits for the previous one to succeed — and it's the one case where a negative offset is mandatory, not optional.

questions.q: How many other triggers can a single tumbling window trigger depend on?
options: A maximum of five
Unlimited
Exactly one
Ten
questions.explain: A tumbling window trigger can depend on up to five other triggers.

questions.q: What does the Gantt view's color coding mean when monitoring trigger dependencies?
options: Blue is pending/running, green means every dependent window succeeded, red means a dependent window failed
All boxes are the same color regardless of status
Red always means the trigger is disabled, not failed
Green means the trigger hasn't started yet
questions.explain: The Gantt view uses transparent boxes for dependency windows (blue while pending/running, green once all succeed, red if one fails) and solid boxes for individual run windows.
